analysis.one_liner: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders is a Mumbai-based, government-owned shipyard that builds warships and submarines for the Indian Navy under long-term defence contracts.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 (quarter ended September 2026) results are due imminently - the company's trading window closed from October 1, 2026 pending the board meeting, so an announcement is expected within days of today. Separately, the ₹70,000-crore Project-75(I) deal to build six advanced stealth submarines with Germany's TKMS has moved to Cabinet Committee on Security approval as of mid-October 2026; if signed, this alone could multiply the current order book several times over.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a defence public sector company that builds ships and submarines almost entirely for the government. The business itself looks strong - no debt, high returns on capital, and profits that have grown with deliveries like INS Mahendragiri and INS Vagir. The tension is that the stock trades at a rich valuation built on the expectation of a giant new submarine order that, as of today, has not yet been formally signed - so a lot of future good news is already priced in, and the stock has fallen sharply from its 2025 peak as that certainty has wavered.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter): revenue rose 12.1% YoY to ₹2,942.7 crore, PAT rose about 21.5% YoY to roughly ₹549-550 crore (sources show ₹549.41 cr and ₹550.46 cr - minor reporting variance), and EBITDA margin expanded sharply from 11.5% to 15.2%, driven by execution efficiency rather than a one-off. Q2 FY26 (September 2025 quarter, last year's comparable): PAT was up 28.1% YoY to ₹749 crore on 6.3% revenue growth. Order book stood at ₹18,218 crore as of June 2026. No non-comparable accounting items flagged in these releases.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is up roughly 1,560% over 5 years and 99% over 3 years - a genuine defence-sector re-rating, not an artifact of the December 2024 2-for-1 split, which is already reflected in these adjusted figures. But it is down 43.8% from its May 2025 peak of ₹3,721 to the current ₹2,092, and down 25.6% over the last year versus Nifty's -9.5%. Against peer Cochin Shipyard, MAZDOCK actually held up better over 1 year (-25.6% vs -29.9%) but has lagged over 3 years (+99% vs +145%) - so the recent relative underperformance is a 1-year phenomenon, not a sustained trend.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 29x (sources range 28.6x-31x depending on date) and P/B of about 8x, the stock sits at a discount to the peer median P/E (~41x) but a premium on P/B. It is expensive because the market is pricing in the possibility of the Project-75(I) submarine order, which could be worth ₹70,000 crore to over ₹1 lakh crore and dwarf the current ₹18,218 crore order book. Whether that is cheap or expensive depends entirely on whether and when that deal is actually signed - as of October 16, 2026 it remained at the Cabinet approval stage, not yet contracted.
analysis.growth_read: Growth looks volume-led and margin-led together, which is the healthier combination: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 12.1% on real deliveries (INS Mahendragiri, INS Vagir), while EBITDA margin simultaneously expanded from 11.5% to 15.2%. This is not a case of flat volumes propped up by cost-cutting alone.
analysis.health_read: The balance sheet carries no debt, and profits appear to convert into cash given consistent free cash flow generation reported alongside ROCE of about 36.5% and ROE of about 27.4%. Financial risk looks minimal; the real risk here is business/execution risk - shipbuilding is a lumpy, contract-dependent business, and revenue visibility hinges on winning and executing large, infrequent government orders rather than on steady repeat demand.
analysis.ownership_read: The promoter is the President of India (the Government of India), holding 81.22% as of September 2026, after the government sold roughly 4% of its stake via an OFS in April 2025 at a floor price of ₹2,525/share. Pledging is not a meaningful concept for a sovereign promoter and was not flagged as an issue in available sources. Public holding is about 12%, FIIs just 1.72%, and mutual funds 1.41% - no marquee independent investor name appears on the register in the data reviewed.
strengths: Debt-free balance sheet with ROCE near 36.5% and ROE near 27.4%
Order book of ₹18,218 crore as of June 2026, backed by real deliveries (INS Mahendragiri, INS Vagir) rather than paper backlog
Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded from 11.5% to 15.2% alongside 12.1% revenue growth - margin and volume moving together
Potential Project-75(I) submarine contract (~₹70,000 crore-plus) now at Cabinet Committee on Security stage, which would be transformative for order visibility if signed
watchpoints: Stock is down 43.8% from its ₹3,721 peak (May 29, 2025) to ₹2,092 now - a real price decline, not a corporate-action distortion
Current ~29x P/E and ~8x P/B already price in significant optimism about Project-75(I); the deal was still unsigned as of October 16, 2026
Government has sold stock via OFS before (April 2025, ~4% stake) and could do so again, creating periodic supply overhang
1-year return of -25.6% has lagged the broader Nifty (-9.5%), even though it beat peer Cochin Shipyard over the same period
analysis.one_thing: Whether and when the Project-75(I) submarine contract with Germany's TKMS is formally signed - this single event would resolve whether the current premium valuation is justified by a multi-fold increase in order book, or whether the stock is pricing in an order that may yet slip or shrink.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 PAT cross-checked across multiple sources (equitybulls, multibagg, investywise) with minor rounding variance (₹549.41 cr vs ₹550.46 cr) - both cited, no single figure averaged. P/E quoted differently across sources (28.6x-31x) depending on date of snapshot; range given rather than a single invented number. Promoter pledge status could not be verified in available sources - noted as not found rather than assumed zero. Exact Q2 FY27 board meeting date could not be confirmed, only that the trading window closure from October 1, 2026 signals an imminent announcement.
